<hypothesis>
To discriminate the top candidates:
- M3 predicts strong nonlinear catalyst dependence (sqrt-like on [cat])
- M4 predicts dependence on a separate species X (not varied—but X is constant; rate is catalytic-type)
- M5 predicts super-linear catalyst dependence (rate ~ [cat]^2 via catS+cat step)
- M9 predicts irreversible catalyst decay (time-dependent loss of activity, but independent of S, P)
- M12 predicts product-enhanced deactivation

A long-time experiment at LOW catalyst with LOW substrate would emphasize deactivation pathways: M9, M12 predict incomplete conversion plateaus. M3 and M5 would achieve full conversion if no deactivation. Using low [cat] also amplifies M3/M5's catalyst-order signatures (M3: rate ~ [cat], not sqrt at low [cat]; M5: rate ~ [cat]^2 becomes small).

Better: use very low catalyst with moderate substrate and zero product. This:
- Tests M9 (time-dependent decay) by examining whether full conversion is reached
- Tests M5's cat^2 dependence (rate should be quite slow)
- Tests M3's behavior (at low [cat], monomer dominates, so looks like M1)
- M12 without initial product: effect builds up only as P forms
- Cleanly separates from prior conditions (iter 2 was high cat; iter 3 had added P)

Low catalyst (~0.002), S=1.0, P=0 probes a new regime.
</hypothesis>
